chunks: Our father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, peace be upon him, who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, when he was taken on the Night Journey to the heavens, did not pass by any creation of Allah except that he saw from it cheerfulness, kindness, and happiness toward him —

until he passed by a creation of Allah who did not turn toward him, nor say anything to him. He found him frowning and scowling. So he said: 'O Jibril, I have not passed by any creation of Allah except that I have seen cheerfulness, kindness, and happiness from it — except this one. Who is this?' He said: 'This is Malik, the keeper of the Fire, and thus did his Lord create him.'

He said: 'I would like you to request of him that he show me the Fire.' So Jibril said to him: 'This is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, and he has asked me to request of you that you show him the Fire.' So he revealed a portion of it for him, and he saw it. And he never smiled broadly again until Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, took him (in death).

key_terms.أُسْرِيَ: Usriya - Was taken on the Night Journey: refers to the miraculous nocturnal journey of the Prophet from Mecca to the heavens
key_terms.افْتَرَّ ضَاحِكًا: Iftarra dahikan - Smiled broadly laughing: a description of uninhibited, open laughter that the Prophet abandoned after witnessing Hell
key_terms.خَازِنُ النَّارِ: Khazin al-Nar - Keeper of the Fire: the angelic custodian of Hellfire, named in Quran 43:77
key_terms.قَاطِبًا عَابِسًا: Qatiban 'abisan - Frowning and scowling: describes Malik's perpetual stern countenance as part of his created nature
key_terms.مَالِكٌ: Malik - The angel appointed as the keeper and guardian of Hellfire, known for his stern nature

ai.seo_question: What happened when the Prophet Muhammad encountered Malik, the keeper of Hellfire, during his Night Journey according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: During the Prophet Muhammad's Night Journey (Isra) to the heavens, every creature he encountered showed him joy, cheerfulness, and kindness — except one. This stern, unsmiling being was Malik, the appointed keeper of Hellfire, whose nature was created that way by God. When the Prophet asked Jibril to request that Malik show him the Fire, Malik revealed a portion of it. After witnessing it, the Prophet never smiled broadly again until his death. This hadith was taught to the early Shi'a community by Imam al-Baqir (d. 114 AH) through his student Zurarah, underscoring the gravity of divine punishment and how the Prophet's direct experience of Hellfire permanently transformed his demeanor.
word_analysis: was taken on the Night Journey

en.bilal-muhammad: 6 - My father (rh) narrated to us, he said: Sa’d ibn ‘Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faddal, from ‘Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as), he said:

When the Messenger of Allah (sw) was taken on the Night Journey to the heavens, he did not pass by any of Allah’s creation except that he saw from them what he loved of joy, kindness, and happiness towards him,

until he passed by one of Allah’s creations, and he did not turn towards him, nor did he say anything to him. He found him frowning and gloomy. He said: 'O Gabriel, I did not pass by any of Allah’s creation except that I saw joy, kindness, and happiness from them except this one, who is this?' He replied: 'This is Malik, the keeper of the Fire, and his Lord has created him this way.'

He said: 'I wish that you ask him to show me the Fire.' Gabriel said to him (Malik): 'This is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, and he has asked me to request you to show him the Fire.' He (Malik) then revealed a part of it to him, and he saw it. From that time, he (the Prophet (sw)) did not smile until Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, took him (in death).
